mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive due to lower real borrowing costs and increased equity discounting.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < mean(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in hourly wage growth (indirect via UNRATE) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment deteriorates.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous 4 weeks AND UNRATE < previous 4 weeks
failure_condition: In 20 out of 40 similar events, the 5-day forward return is non-negative (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in consumer confidence (proxied by HOUST) above 1700 for two consecutive months is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it signals robust consumer spending.
failure_condition: During 10 analogous high-HOUST periods, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly higher than the baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 101.0 for three consecutive months, while inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 280, predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days due to supply-side weakness.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 101.0 for 3 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 280
failure_condition: In 15 analogous contractionary INDPRO-CPIAUCSL regimes, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in more than 70% of cases (binomial p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 285 for two consecutive months triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as markets anticipate rate hikes that erode equity valuations.
failure_condition: Over 10 such episodes, the 5-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 4% (UNRATE < 4.0) and remains stable for 4 consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return tends to be positive due to strong labor market resilience and optimism in equity valuations.
failure_condition: Across 8 such regimes, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly higher than the prior 60-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both retail sales (implied via PAYEMS) and manufacturing activity (RSAFS) below their 12-month moving averages for 3 months predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days due to dual demand weakness.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 12mo_mavg AND RSAFS < 12mo_mavg for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 12 analogous dual-signal weakness regimes, the 20-day forward return is not negative in more than 40% of cases (binomial p < 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer spending (HOUST) below 1600 for 5 consecutive months in a low-rate environment (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days due to persistent demand weakness despite accommodative policy.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 1600 for 5 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 1.0% for last 3 months
failure_condition: During 7 analogous regimes, the 60-day forward return is not negative in more than 50% of cases (binomial p < 0.05).
